cards.text: This is the prophet Isaiah talking to God's people. He's just described the Lord GOD of Hosts cutting down the tall trees and clearing the forest thickets with an axe. Picture a whole hillside of stumps, like that forest just got the WORST haircut in history.
Then Isaiah zooms in on one stump, the stump of Jesse, King David's father (Ruth 4:22). That's not a family tree anymore, friend, that's a family coaster.

cards.question: Out of the stump of Jesse, what does Isaiah say will spring up?
True or false: Isaiah says the Branch growing from Jesse's roots will wither away.

cards.text: And this Branch is no ordinary plant, because Isaiah calls it Him. The Spirit of the LORD will rest on Him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and strength, knowledge and fear of the LORD.

cards.question: The Spirit of the fear of the LORD rests on the Branch, and Isaiah says He will ___ in the fear of the LORD.

cards.text: Now Isaiah gets to how He will judge. Which is good news, because I judge cookies by looks, and friend, I have burnt a LOT of cookies that looked PERFECT.

cards.question: True or false: the Branch will judge by what His eyes see and decide by what His ears hear.
The Branch won't judge by looks or by what He hears. Isaiah says He will judge the ___ with righteousness.

cards.text: With equity He will decide for the lowly of the earth. Then Isaiah says He will strike the earth and slay the wicked.

cards.question: What does the Branch strike the earth with?

answers.text: An iron rod in His hand

cards.text: And He slays the wicked with the breath of His lips. Just words? Friend, I've been yelling at my oven for YEARS, and it has never once baked faster.

cards.question: Isaiah describes what the Branch wears, and righteousness is the belt around His hips. True or false: faithfulness is part of His outfit too.

cards.text: Then the picture gets WILD. I mean literally wild, as in animals, starting with a wolf and a lamb.

cards.question: True or false: in Isaiah's picture, the wolf hunts down the lamb.
The leopard lies down with the goat, and the calf, the young lion and the fatling are all together. Who leads this whole crowd?

cards.text: The cow grazes with the bear, and their young lie down together. A bear. Grazing. Next to a cow. Friend, that bear's out there acting like he's never even HEARD of a cow.

cards.question: Then Isaiah gets to the lion. True or false: in this picture, the lion eats straw like the ox.

cards.text: The infant plays by the cobra's den, and the toddler reaches into the viper's nest. Friend, I flinch when my oven timer goes off, and this toddler's reaching into a VIPER'S NEST.

cards.question: In Isaiah's picture, why is a toddler safe near a viper's nest?

answers.text: Nothing harms on God's holy mountain
The vipers have all been driven out
Guards stand watch over the child

cards.question: Here's why nothing harms or destroys there: the earth will be full of the ___ of the ___, as the sea is full of water.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says, "On that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples." Picture it lifted high, like the OPEN sign I flip on at my bakery every single morning.

cards.question: The Root of Jesse stands as a banner for the peoples, and the ___ will seek Him.

cards.text: And His place of rest will be glorious. Years later, Paul points back to Isaiah and the Root of Jesse while writing about Christ, the One who pulled me out of the dark (Romans 15:8-12).
On that day the Lord reaches out His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people. The list of places runs from Assyria and Egypt all the way to the islands of the sea.

cards.question: The Lord raises a banner for the nations and gathers the exiles of Israel. And the scattered of Judah? Where does He collect them from?

answers.text: The four corners of the earth
The far side of the Jordan
The plains of Moab near Jericho

cards.text: Then come two old rivals, Ephraim and Judah, split apart since the day Ephraim separated from Judah (Isaiah 7:17). They remind me of the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, arguing for YEARS over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says Ephraim will keep envying Judah, and Judah will keep harassing Ephraim.

cards.text: Now they swoop down on the Philistines to the west, and together they plunder the sons of the east. Then the LORD sweeps His hand over the Euphrates with a scorching wind and splits it into seven streams.

cards.question: True or false: once the LORD splits the Euphrates into seven streams, people can cross it with dry sandals.
Isaiah says there will be a highway for the remnant of God's people coming from Assyria. What earlier journey does he compare it to?

answers.text: When Israel came up from Egypt
When Abram set out from Ur

cards.text: Now Isaiah tells his listeners what they will say in that day. It starts, "O LORD, I will praise You."

cards.question: The speaker says the LORD was angry. What has happened to that anger now?
True or false: the speaker says the LORD has brought comfort.

cards.text: Then the speaker says, surely God is my salvation. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer holding my breath every time it opened, so this next part hits me RIGHT here.

cards.question: Because God is the speaker's salvation, what does the speaker decide to do?

cards.text: The speaker goes on: the LORD GOD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation. My strength? A mustache that can carry three cookie boxes. This speaker is doing MUCH better than I am.
Then Isaiah paints a picture of drawing water from the springs of salvation.

cards.question: In Isaiah's picture, they draw water from the springs of salvation with ___.

cards.text: And on that day there's a second thing to say. Give praise to the LORD and proclaim His name!

cards.question: In this second thing they will say on that day, where should the LORD's works be made known?
True or false: these words say the glorious things the LORD has done should be kept quiet.

cards.text: The last line goes out to the citizen of Zion: cry out and sing! That's Mags-level volume, friend, the WHOLE kitchen's gonna hear it.

cards.question: True or false: the last line tells the citizen of Zion that the Holy One of Israel is far away from them.
